correctness.rationale: A complete partition of the high quotient a=floor(n/2^r) shows that neither a=U 0^e 1^j with j>0 (consecutive interior zero lengths e and e−1) nor j=0 (incompatible terminal zero parities) can produce two admissible indices. Thus a=2^(2t)−1 and the shared r-bit suffix is tiled by 1 and 00. The cutoff 2t+r<m is exact; |T_r|=F_{r+1}. The derivation explicitly handles r=0, n=0, and end-of-window conditions. Direct complete paired-index sets through m=15 and independent bitwise carry transfer counts through m=60 agree, without being substituted for the infinite proof.

Automatic sequence pseudorandomness papers supply different correlation bounds; historic support records supply membership and its Fibonacci growth, not the sharp pair classification. residual_risks: Potential historical equivalent result under ordered self-generating-set or automatic-sequence correlations is not ruled out by indexed sources.
The 1976 foundational paper is bibliographically verified but its full text was unavailable for inspection.
The OEIS original-entry date anchors the first day-verified cited source; the original 1976 work predates it but has no verified initial-public calendar day in the consulted evidence.

value.rationale: This is the full natural two-parameter dyadic autocorrelation family of a classical sparse automatic set: it identifies every pair, computes all finite dyadic correlations, and distinguishes fixed-shift logarithmic growth from macroscopic shifts with Fibonacci mass. The key binary carry rigidity is structural and the invariant is not supplied by adjacent-gap histograms; its usefulness is a sharp benchmark for sparse automatic support self-overlap, not an arbitrary finite slice or unsupported application.
